clinical: Atherosclerosis starts in the intima, where LDL cholesterol collects beneath a damaged endothelium and forms fatty streaks that can grow into plaques.
Smoking, high blood pressure and high LDL cholesterol all injure the endothelium and reduce its nitric oxide release, an early step in atherosclerosis.

Tunica media.description: The tunica media is the thick middle coat of an elastic artery. It is made of repeated lamellar units: a sheet of elastin with smooth muscle cells, collagen and ground substance between each pair of sheets. The smooth muscle cells make the elastin and collagen, and the elastic sheets stretch in systole and recoil in diastole to keep blood flowing.
clinical: Marfan syndrome, caused by a fibrillin-1 defect, weakens the elastic lamellae of the media, causing cystic medial degeneration, aortic dilation and a risk of dissection.
With age and long-standing hypertension the elastic lamellae fragment and the aorta stiffens, which raises systolic pressure and pulse pressure.

Tunica adventitia.description: The tunica adventitia is the outer coat of the aorta, made of connective tissue: wavy type I collagen bundles with elastic fibres, fibroblasts, nerves and small vessels. Its collagen limits how far the wall can stretch. The aortic wall is too thick to be fed from the lumen alone, so small vessels called vasa vasorum run through the outer wall to supply it.
clinical: When an aneurysm or dissection tears through the adventitia, blood escapes into the pericardium, mediastinum or pleural cavity, which is life-threatening.
Tertiary syphilis inflames the vasa vasorum of the ascending aorta; the resulting loss of medial elastic tissue weakens the wall and can produce an aneurysm.
Red cells lose their biconcave shape and become spherical, so the spleen removes them early, causing haemolytic anaemia.
Defective beta-2 integrins stop leukocytes from sticking to the endothelium and leaving the blood, so affected patients get recurrent bacterial infections.
